findings.description: In the continuous sunlit wide shot (1:50.2 onward) there is only one waitress, who rises from a stool and leans over the counter at 1:51. At ~1:52 a second figure with identical wardrobe (light-blue uniform, white apron, hair in bun) materialises at the back-left end of the counter while the first waitress simultaneously walks behind the counter on the right; both are visible together through ~1:55, after which one fades away. No cut and no entrance explains a second identical person.

Within the single wide shot starting 1:17.6, the waitress stands behind the counter (service side) facing the trucker at 1:20-1:21.0. By 1:21.25 she is on the customer side directly beside him, with legs visible on the stool side, having passed through the counter in ~0.25 s with no path around it. She then also reads noticeably smaller/childlike in scale next to him (1:22-1:26) compared with her earlier standing size.

At 0:27 in the same wide camera setup the trucker sits on a stool on the customer side at the counter curve, facing screen-right toward the waitress. After the food inserts, the 0:36.5 wide shot shows him at a different spot further right, facing straight to camera with his torso on the service side of the counter and his legs on the stool side, i.e., straddling/inside the counter where the waitress had stood; the stools beside him are empty. His position and facing change without visible movement and the new placement is physically implausible.

At 1:50.167 the waitress is standing at a booth window (ketchup/mustard on the table) looking down, with the trucker still at his truck outside; at the 1:50.208 cut she is instead seated on a counter stool across the room with a mug, with no intervening shot to cover the move. Possible intended time-skip, but the cut gives no cue of elapsed time.
